html:
A great Mughal mosque in Lahore, Pakistan, built from 1671 to 1673 by the emperor Aurangzeb, facing the Lahore Fort.

It is the last of the great imperial mosques of the Mughal Empire, built of red sandstone with white marble domes and four tall corner minarets. Its courtyard holds tens of thousands of worshippers. For more than three centuries it was one of the largest mosques in the world.

Its later history follows Lahore's. When the Sikh Empire of Ranjit Singh ruled the city, the mosque was used as a stable and garrison. The British also used it as a barracks before returning it to Muslims for worship in the 1850s and later. Major repairs from the 1930s restored it. The poet Muhammad Iqbal is buried beside its gateway. Today it is one of the best known landmarks of Pakistan.
sum: A great Mughal mosque in Lahore, Pakistan, built from 1671 to 1673 by the emperor Aurangzeb, facing the Lahore Fort.
